text.p: The Turkish central bank lent banks 19.9 trillion lira overnight at 80 percent on the interbank on Thursday after the money market opened 25 trillion lira short, compared to the 25 trillion it funded on Wednesday.
Overnight money also traded at 79.75 percent.
The lira closed easier at 99,530 against the dollar versus Wednesday's 99,350 on higher central bank dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign exchange transfers, despite banks' dollar sales.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory forex transfers at 99,350 lira at the open, up from Wednesday's close at 99,250 lira. It further raised the rate to 99,500 lira in the afternoon on higher dollar-mark parity.
Bankers said dollar demand which has been firm in the last two weeks, prompting frequent central bank intervention, weakened after the central bank raised its overnight rates on Wednesday.
The bank had raised its overnight bid and offer rates to 55-80 percent from 50-75 percent to support the lira yesterday.
Yields on T-bills and bonds with longer maturities eased one-to-three points on buying, others were steady.
Dealers said banks began buying paper on Wednesday when the the Treasury issued only 51.49 trillion lira worth May 21, 1997 bills in return for 135.6 trillion lira of maturing bills.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper eased to 123.35 from Wednesday's 125.38. The second most active May 21, 1997 paper yielded 123.67 average down from Wednesday's 126.38 percent average.
